title: branches without fear
goal: B1 Create, switch, compare and delete branches
startWith: Back in git-lab. Branches are cheap here — break them.

newIdeas.plain: A movable name pointing at a commit. Creating one copies nothing.
You are on a commit, not a branch. Commits made here are reachable only by hash.
A merge with nothing to merge: the branch pointer just slides forward.

tasks.do: Create a branch, commit on it, and switch back
tasks.why: switch and restore replaced the overloaded checkout for exactly this reason: one verb, one job.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git switch -c feature/greeting
echo 'hello' > greeting.txt
git add -A && git commit -m "add greeting"
git switch -
ls          # greeting.txt is gone: it lives on the other branch

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Ctrl+Shift+` (Git → Branches) is the branch popup: new, switch, compare, delete, all from one list. The current branch also shows bottom-right in the status bar.

check.expect: the branch you switched back to

tasks.do: List branches, and see which are merged

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git branch -vv
git branch --merged
git branch --no-merged

tasks.do: Compare two branches before merging either way
tasks.why: “What would this merge bring in” is a question with an exact answer.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git log --oneline main..feature/greeting   # in feature, not in main
git log --oneline feature/greeting..main   # the other direction
git diff main...feature/greeting           # the change the branch makes

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Branch popup → the branch → Compare with Current shows exactly these two lists side by side.

tasks.do: Merge with a fast-forward, then merge with a real merge commit
tasks.why: Seeing both makes --no-ff a choice instead of folklore.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git switch main && git merge feature/greeting          # fast-forward
git log --oneline --graph -5
git switch -c feature/second && echo x > x.txt && git add -A && git commit -m second
git switch main && git merge --no-ff feature/second    # merge commit
git log --oneline --graph -5

tasks.do: Delete a merged branch, then try to delete an unmerged one
tasks.why: -d refuses to lose work; -D does not. The refusal is the feature.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git branch -d feature/greeting
git switch -c throwaway && echo y > y.txt && git add -A && git commit -m tmp && git switch main
git branch -d throwaway     # refused
git branch -D throwaway     # forced — still recoverable from the reflog, step 05

proof.expect: a graph with one merge commit in it
proof.note: You can read your own history graph.

doneWhen: You create a branch per unit of work without thinking about it.

lessons.title: Branch popup (Ctrl+Shift+`)
lessons.teach: Ctrl+Shift+` lists every local and remote branch with search. New branch, switch, rename, compare with current, delete — the whole of step 03 lives in this one popup.
